name: Avalon Emerson
label: Another Dove
lede: She wrote software by day, threw SoMa warehouse parties by night, became a Panorama Bar regular, then turned up at a London pub with a cellist, a guitarist and a debut album of songs she sang herself.

eras.title: Code by day, warehouses by night
eras.text: Born in San Francisco and raised in Arizona, Avalon Emerson worked as a software developer while DJing and throwing warehouse parties in the city. Her first records came out that year on two local labels.

years.src: Wikipedia: Avalon Emerson · Crack Magazine: Cover story · DJ Mag: Avalon Emerson
years.h: Three records in a year on Icee Hot and Spring Theory
years.p: Emerson's first releases were "Pressure / Quoi!" on Icee Hot, then "Church of SoMa" and "Let Me Love & Steal / Honest Gangster" on Spring Theory, all while she held a software job.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists all three as 2014 releases, and Crack describes the sound as chunky, sample-driven and leaning on DFA-style dance-punk. She had been making edits before she made originals.

DJ Mag reports she left San Francisco in the mid-2010s in part because she disliked the tech industry's "bro culture". Wikipedia dates her move to Berlin to 2014.

eras.title: The Frontier
eras.text: Berlin, Panorama Bar, and a track that Resident Advisor would later put in its top 10 of the decade. Whities and Spectral Sound co-signed her, and she went full-time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Avalon Emerson · DJ Mag: Avalon Emerson · Crack Magazine: Cover story
years.h: "The Frontier" lands on Whities and won't leave
years.p: Whities 006 paired "The Frontier" with "2000 Species of Cacti". Resident Advisor later named "The Frontier" one of the top 10 tracks of the decade, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
DJ Mag describes the track's cloud-skimming melody. The same year she also put out "Narcissus in Retrograde" on Spectral Sound. Crack says those two co-signs are what pushed her to pause the tech career.

DJ Mag reports she lived in Berlin for six years before the pandemic and learned to DJ at Panorama Bar, which she calls a "gay mecca for our age".

years.h: A Mondo Disko set from the Berlin years
years.p: Live footage of Emerson mixing in 2016, the year the club circuit caught up with her.

years.h: She remixes Slowdive, then Christine and the Queens, Robyn, Four Tet
years.p: Emerson's remix of Slowdive's "Sugar for the Pill" came in 2017; the list that followed runs through Christine and the Queens (2018), Four Tet (2019), Robyn (2020) and King Princess (2021).
years.xp:
Before any of that she circulated free bootleg edits she called Cybernedits, which she stopped distributing in 2016, according to Wikipedia. The 2017 Whities release "One More Fluorescent Rush" came the same year.

Shoegaze, synth-pop and a techno DJ's hands on the stems: it is the clearest early hint of where the Charm would end up.

eras.title: Thirty-three countries and a cover song
eras.text: The touring peak, a Bandcamp side project, and a DJ-Kicks mix that opened with her singing. Then the pandemic took the road away.

years.h: Buy Music Club starts as a Bandcamp list site
years.p: Emerson co-launched Buy Music Club, a site for building and sharing lists of music on Bandcamp, with friends; FACT covered the launch in December.

years.src: Crack Magazine: Cover story · Dazed: Avalon Emerson · DJ Mag: Avalon Emerson
years.p: Crack reports Emerson played in 33 countries across six continents in 2019 and was already planning to tour less to be closer to family.
years.xp: In the Dazed track-by-track for her DJ-Kicks she said she went through "a pretty unshakable bout of anxiety and climate/future-related depression for a large part of 2019". DJ Mag quotes her saying "I was approaching burnout, for sure".

years.src: Dazed: Avalon Emerson · Crack Magazine: Cover story
years.h: DJ-Kicks opens with her singing a Magnetic Fields song
years.p: Her DJ-Kicks mix for !K7 starts with her own version of the Magnetic Fields' "Long Forgotten Fairytale", her first sung vocal on record.
years.xp:
She began the cover at Bullion's studio in Lisbon, inspired by the cover albums on his DEEK label, and finished it in Los Angeles with what she called "a bit of a tougher beat", per Dazed.

Dazed notes she picked it as the surprising opening track.

years.src: Crack Magazine: Cover story · DJ Mag: Avalon Emerson · Stereogum: Band To Watch · Resident Advisor: & the Charm review · Wikipedia: & the Charm
years.h: Lockdown sends her and Hunter Lombard to the Catskills
years.p: Crack says she moved to Los Angeles with her partner just before COVID spread, then drove east to be nearer to family; Resident Advisor places the album's writing in the Catskills.
years.xp:
Sources disagree on where the record was started. Wikipedia says Emerson began it in 2020 at her Los Angeles home with her wife Hunter Lombard, and Stereogum says her first song came from goofing around on a synth with Lombard there.

DJ Mag has her in rural upstate New York, working from the spiritual inspiration of The Postal Service's 2003 album Give Up.

eras.title: I'm not a new artist, I'm just a new band
eras.text: Emerson starts Another Dove with Nic Tasker, teams up with Bullion, and puts out a nine-track album under her name and the Charm.

years.h: Eternal September with Anunaku, as A+A
years.p: Emerson and Anunaku put out the dance-floor record Eternal September on AD 93, the label formerly known as Whities.

years.src: The Fader: Song You Need · Stereogum: Band To Watch
years.h: "Sandrail Silhouette" is the first Charm single
years.p: The Fader ran it as a Song You Need; Emerson told Stereogum she worried it was too small to be a song until Bullion proved otherwise within a day.

years.src: Mixmag: Beauty amid the chaos · MusicTech: Avalon Emerson finds her voice · Stereogum: Band To Watch
years.h: The Charm play a pub in East London
years.p: Emerson, Hunter Lombard on guitar and Keivon Hobeheidar on cello and bass played their first public show at the Shacklewell Arms, per Mixmag.
years.xp:
MusicTech lists the rig: Ableton Live with stem triggering, a MIDI stomp box, amp modellers for bass and cello, in-ear monitors and a light show. Emerson told them "I'm not a new artist, I'm just a new band."

She told Stereogum that stage adrenaline was something she hadn't felt DJing in a long time.

years.src: Wikipedia: & the Charm · Mixmag: Beauty amid the chaos · Why Now: Avalon Emerson · Resident Advisor: & the Charm review
years.h: & the Charm: nine songs, one nine-minute closer
years.p: Released on Another Dove and co-produced with Bullion, it ends on "A Dam Will Always Divide", which runs nearly nine minutes.
years.xp:
Another Dove was co-founded by Emerson and Nic Tasker, per Mixmag and Why Now. Wikipedia lists One House Records alongside it for the release.

Resident Advisor's Sophie McNulty wrote that Emerson ducks out of dance music and resurfaces in an indie rock band, and that the dance history only shows in the second half, on "Hot Evening".

years.src: Wikipedia: & the Charm · Album of the Year
years.h: Pitchfork gives it 8.0 and ranks it No. 30 of 2023
years.p: Anna Gaca's Pitchfork review used those words for the turn from techno DJ to songwriter. Pitchfork put the album 30th on its 50 best of 2023.
years.xp:
Score per Wikipedia and Album of the Year, which also lists Pitchfork's review as 80/100. Wikipedia reports Exclaim! placed it 17th and Gorilla vs. Bear 19th on their year-end lists.

Gaca's review named Japanese city pop, shoegaze and Balearic house among the influences, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Second album, bigger label
eras.text: Same band and producer, new label, and Rostam Batmanglij in the room.

years.h: Written into Changes arrives on Dead Oceans
years.p: The second Avalon Emerson & the Charm album is co-produced by Bullion and Rostam Batmanglij, with Jay Flew added to the circle.
years.xp:
Dead Oceans lists recording in Braintree, England in winter and spring 2024, plus Los Angeles and Glendale, California. Singles included "Eden", "Written into Changes" and "Jupiter and Mars".

Emerson's own line in the release: making it "felt like unlocking a fence and running into a big green field".
